question: Which built-in Python data structures, function features and file operations does a data analyst need before using pandas and NumPy?
contributions: Functions, scope, lambdas, partial application, generators, itertools, exceptions
File objects, modes, bytes versus Unicode

results.claim: count on a tuple returns the number of occurrences of a value (2 occurs 4 times in the example).
bisect.bisect(c, 2) on the sorted list returns insertion index 4, bisect(c, 5) returns 6.
A generator expression sums squares of 0..99 lazily to 328350.
Reading 10 characters of UTF-8 text with an n-tilde moves the file position to byte 11, not 10.

limits: Targets Python 3.6-era; no performance measurements, only qualitative claims (insert vs append, list + vs extend, list membership linear vs hash constant).
Dict ordering is described as unordered; later Python versions preserve insertion order, so that statement has dated.
Bare except in attempt_float shown first; author then narrows it.
practices: Use extend rather than + to build a large list, since + creates a new list and copies objects (p.56).
Prefer collections.deque if inserting at both ends of a sequence, since list insert is expensive (p.55).
Use dict or set for membership tests; list membership is a linear scan (p.56).
Do not use bisect on an unsorted list; it does not check and gives wrong results silently (p.58).
Use defaultdict(list) or setdefault instead of if/else when grouping into dict of lists (p.64).
Keys of dicts and elements of sets must be hashable; convert lists to tuples (p.64-66).
Discourage the global keyword; many globals suggest using classes (p.71).
Apply a list of functions to clean strings, giving a reusable generic cleaner (p.72-73).
Catch specific exceptions (ValueError, or a tuple of types) so real bugs like TypeError still surface (p.78).
Use finally or a with block so files are always closed (p.78, p.81).
Keep nested comprehensions to two or three levels for readability (p.69).
Beware seek in text mode; landing mid-character raises UnicodeDecodeError (p.84).
